name: Shift Coaching
shortDescription: Encourages CRCA pastors to build intentional peer, elder, and ministry coaching relationships around pastoral health and disciple-making.
fullDescription: Overseen by the TRAIN Workgroup and Ministry Development Coordinator, Shift Coaching invites pastors and Church Councils into structured reflection across five key rhythms: Love One Another, Discipleship, Multiplying Leadership, Reaching the Lost, and Professional Development.

name: Local Church Outreach Training
shortDescription: Equips everyday church members to share the gospel naturally through cohorts, coaching, and a partnership with Organic Outreach International.
fullDescription: Through cohorts, practical evangelism resources, and ongoing coaching, Local Church Outreach Training helps congregations build a culture where outreach flows naturally from everyday relationships and local community engagement.

name: Missional Explorations
shortDescription: Provides matching seed grants up to $2,500 to help local churches bridge everyday outreach and formal church planting.
fullDescription: Supported by the Church Planting Taskforce (CPT), Missional Explorations helps emerging church-planting teams fund core-team training, hospitality, equipment, venue hire, and outreach materials as they test new gospel initiatives.
highlights: Up to $2,500 matching seed funding from CPT

name: Church Planting Taskforce (CPT)
shortDescription: Encourages, researches, and resources new CRCA church plants and congregation revitalisation efforts across Australia.
fullDescription: The Church Planting Taskforce works across states and classes to research unreached regions, refine church planting and revitalisation models, develop financial sustainability, and oversee Missional Explorations grants.

name: Candidacy Committee
shortDescription: Guides aspiring pastors through theological training, mentoring, vicariate placement, and Classis examination toward ordained CRCA ministry.
fullDescription: The Candidacy Committee oversees four ordination pathways and an 11-step approval journey—typically encouraging study at the Reformed Theological College (RTC) followed by a supervised one-year vicariate in a local congregation.

name: Reformed Theological College (RTC)
shortDescription: Provides accredited, biblically faithful Reformed theological education preparing pastors, missionaries, and ministry leaders.
fullDescription: Located in Victoria and serving students across Australia and online, RTC partners closely with the CRCA to form men and women grounded in Scripture, Reformed confessions, and pastoral wisdom.

name: CRCA Cadets
shortDescription: Equips boys and mentors across local congregations to live for Christ through Scripture study, outdoor adventure, and service projects.
fullDescription: Part of the Christian Cadet Corps network, local CRCA Cadet clubs pair faithful men from the church with primary and early-high-school boys for hands-on badges, camping, and biblical character formation.

name: CRCA GEMS Girls' Clubs
shortDescription: Creates welcoming club communities where girls discover God's love, build lasting friendships, and grow as disciples of Jesus.
fullDescription: GEMS (Girls Everywhere Meeting the Saviour) connects mentors and girls in local congregations through Bible discovery, worship, crafts, camps, and practical community care.

name: CRCA Youth Convention
shortDescription: Brings Reformed teenagers and young adults from across Australia together for biblical teaching, worship, and lifelong fellowship.
fullDescription: A flagship national gathering where high-schoolers and young leaders explore Scripture deeply, build friendships beyond their home state, and catch a bigger vision for God's kingdom.

name: Safe Church Unit
shortDescription: Supports congregations with safeguarding policies, Working With Children compliance, leadership training, and pastoral care guidance.
fullDescription: Committed to protecting children and vulnerable people in every CRCA congregation, the Safe Church Unit provides national standards, screening protocols, training workshops, and confidential advice for elders and ministry teams.

name: World Transform
shortDescription: Oversees CRCA international mission partnerships bringing holistic gospel word and community transformation across partner nations.
fullDescription: Working alongside local church partners overseas, World Transform supports gospel ministry, leadership training, compassion initiatives, and long-term cross-cultural mission.

name: Solomon Islands SWIM
shortDescription: Supports indigenous church life, leadership equipping, and practical community ministry at the SWIM mission base in the Solomon Islands.
fullDescription: SWIM (Supporting Work in Ministry) is an overseas mission arm of the CRCA connecting Australian congregations with believers in the Solomon Islands through mutual encouragement, training, community partnerships, and short-term mission teams.

name: Ecumenical Relations
shortDescription: Maintains sister-church fellowship with Reformed denominations worldwide and represents the CRCA within the ICRC.
fullDescription: Under Church Order Article 52, this three-member synodical committee fosters unity and mutual encouragement with sister churches across Australia and around the globe.
highlights: Ecclesiastical Fellowship: Presbyterian Church of Eastern Australia, Reformed Churches of New Zealand, Orthodox Presbyterian Church (USA), Reformed Churches in South Africa
International Member: International Conference of Reformed Churches (ICRC)
Other Reformed Contacts: Presbyterian Church of Australia, Westminster Presbyterian Church (Australia), Reformed Presbyterian Church (Australia), URCNA
